title: Career Roadmap: Data Analyst
summary: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, examines and interprets data to help organizations understand trends, measure performance and make informed decisions. Graduates of integrated M.Sc. programmes in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biotechnology or Life Sciences can enter data analytics by combining their scientific and quantitative knowledge with programming, statistics, visualization and business communication.

facts.Current degree: Integrated / Dual-Degree Programmes (BS-MS, B.Tech+M.Tech, B.Sc-M.Sc, BA-MA)
facts.Course: Integrated M.Sc (Physics / Chemistry / Maths / Biotech / Life Sciences)

blocks.text: A Data Analyst collects, cleans, examines and interprets data to help organizations understand trends, measure performance and make informed decisions. Graduates of integrated M.Sc. programmes in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biotechnology or Life Sciences can enter data analytics by combining their scientific and quantitative knowledge with programming, statistics, visualization and business communication.
Core responsibility
Turn raw data into meaningful insights, dashboards, reports and recommendations.
Relevant sectors
IT, banking, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, scientific research, manufacturing, consulting and business operations.

rows.text: Integrated M.Sc. in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biotechnology or Life Sciences
Often 5 years; confirm the institution's programme structure
Statistics, quantitative reasoning, scientific methods and subject-specific data interpretation
Excel, SQL, Python, data visualization and basic statistical analysis
Internships, research-data projects, dashboards and portfolio development
Optional specialization in analytics, statistics, business analytics, data science or bioinformatics

blocks.text: An integrated M.Sc. can provide a strong analytical foundation, but students should separately develop practical data tools and demonstrate their abilities through projects. Most general data analyst roles do not require a PhD.
Years 1–2
Build quantitative foundations

items.text: Strengthen mathematics, probability, statistics and logical reasoning.
Learn Excel, spreadsheet formulas and data organization.
Understand research methods and scientific data collection.
Practise interpreting tables, graphs and experimental results.

blocks.text: Years 3–4
Develop analytics skills

items.text: Learn SQL for retrieving and filtering data.
Learn Python with pandas, NumPy and matplotlib.
Build dashboards using Power BI or Tableau.
Apply statistics to scientific datasets and business problems.

blocks.text: Year 5
Prepare for employment

items.text: Complete an analytics-focused dissertation or internship.
Build three to five well-documented portfolio projects.
Practise SQL queries, data interpretation and case-study interviews.
Apply for Data Analyst, Junior Data Analyst and Research Data Analyst positions.

rows.text: Statistical analysis, forecasting and quantitative analytics
Scientific computing, experimental data and engineering analytics
Laboratory analytics, quality control and chemical research data
Clinical research data, biological datasets and public-health analytics

blocks.text: These are possible directions rather than automatic career outcomes. Specialized roles may require additional domain knowledge, experience or postgraduate qualifications.
Students should seek internships with analytics teams, research laboratories, healthcare organizations, pharmaceutical companies, consulting firms and business intelligence teams.
Recommended portfolio projects

blocks.label: Sales dashboard
blocks.text: Analyze revenue, product performance and monthly trends using SQL and Power BI.

blocks.label: Scientific experiment analysis
blocks.text: Clean a laboratory dataset, summarize measurements and visualize relationships.

blocks.label: Healthcare data analysis
blocks.text: Explore a public health dataset, identify patterns and explain limitations.

blocks.label: Customer behaviour analysis
blocks.text: Use SQL to segment customers and calculate retention metrics.

blocks.label: Research-data project
blocks.text: Analyse a publicly available scientific dataset relevant to the student's M.Sc. subject.

Each project should include a clear question, data source, cleaning process, analysis, visualizations, conclusions and limitations. Use public or properly authorized data and avoid exposing confidential information.
Useful tools include:

blocks.label: Excel
blocks.text: PivotTables, lookup functions and data cleaning.

blocks.label: SQL
blocks.text: Filtering, joins, aggregation, subqueries and window functions.

blocks.label: Python
blocks.text: pandas, NumPy, matplotlib and seaborn.

blocks.label: Power BI or Tableau
blocks.text: Interactive dashboards and reporting.

blocks.label: Git and GitHub
blocks.text: Project version control and portfolio presentation.

Optional training can include introductory SQL, Python for data analysis, statistics, Power BI and domain-specific analytics. Select courses with practical assignments rather than relying only on certificates.
Analytics Intern
Learn data cleaning, reporting and analysis
Junior Data Analyst
Prepare datasets, queries, reports and dashboards
Data Analyst / Senior Data Analyst
Own analyses, interpret trends and support decisions
Analytics Lead / BI Analyst / Data Scientist
Potential progression through experience and further specialization

Progression depends on practical skills, project impact, communication, industry experience and the requirements of the target role. Moving into data science generally requires deeper programming, statistical modelling and machine-learning knowledge.
AI tools can accelerate routine work, but analysts still need to validate outputs, understand statistical limitations and communicate evidence accurately.
Preparation progress
Build strong statistics and quantitative reasoning skills
Learn Excel and SQL
Learn Python for data analysis
Create dashboards using Power BI or Tableau
Complete at least three portfolio projects
Complete an internship or practical research project
Prepare a résumé and practise analytics interviews

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Students pursuing an integrated M.Sc. should combine their scientific or mathematical strengths with SQL, Python, statistics and data visualization. Build a portfolio using real datasets, gain practical experience and target entry-level analyst roles aligned with the subject expertise they develop during their degree.
